prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but to give a useful recommendation I need a little more detail. Quick questions:

- Do you need an individual/family ACA plan (marketplace), short-term coverage, or something else (dental, supplemental, Medicare)?
- Do you want an in-person/local agent in Kansas City, MO, or are you okay with an online/national broker?
- Rough annual household income (or whether you expect to qualify for premium tax credits)?
- Any carrier preferences or medical needs (preferred doctors, meds)?

While you answer, a few quick guidelines and reliable options:

What to look for in a broker for the self-employed
- Independent (represents multiple carriers) so you get comparisions.
- Experience with ACA/individual market and subsidy enrollment.
- Transparent about whether they charge a fee (many consumer-facing brokers are paid by carriers).
- Good reviews and responsive customer service (important at renewal time).
- Will help with eligibility for premium tax credits and cost-sharing differences, not just monthly premium.

National / online options that work well for self-employed people
- HealthSherpa — focuses on ACA marketplace enrollment and subsidies; easy to compare marketplace plans.
- eHealth — large national broker that compares multiple carriers (both marketplace and off-exchange options).
- Stride Health — geared toward gig/self-employed workers; helpful tools for benefits and tax considerations.

If you want a local, in-person agent in Kansas City, MO
- I can look up top-rated independent agents/agencies near you (with ratings and specialties) if you share your ZIP code or neighborhood. I’ll compare 3–4 and show who specializes in individual/ACA plans, client reviews, and contact info.

Tell me the answers to the questions above (or your ZIP code) and I’ll find 3 recommended brokers/agents tailored to your needs.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
